source.title: Mentoring posts for young African entrepreneurs
source.attribution: Summary in our own words of Strive Masiyiwa's mentoring posts for young African entrepreneurs on Facebook. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author.
source.notes: Original summary written by Reborn; contains no text from the posts, which are in copyright. Ideas confirmed via news coverage (The Standard, Kenya; News Ghana; Fox News/AP) because the posts themselves sit behind a Facebook login.

cards.title: Learn the rules and language of your field
cards.body:
Masiyiwa tells young entrepreneurs that every industry has its own rules, terms and ways of doing things. If you don't understand them, established players won't take you seriously and doors stay closed.

Taking time to master that language, through reading, courses, mentors and listening carefully, gives you credibility and access to the networks where deals happen. It's an investment that pays off whichever sector you enter.
cards.apply_it: List five terms or rules in your field you only half-understand, and learn one properly this week.

quiz.question: Why does Masiyiwa stress learning an industry's rules and language?
options: It earns credibility and access to established networks
So you can ignore them later
quiz.explanation: Understanding how a field works lets newcomers be taken seriously and gain access.

cards.title: Be willing to say no to bribes, even at a cost
cards.body:
In widely shared posts, Masiyiwa wrote that he has never paid a bribe and has turned down demands from powerful people, sometimes losing contracts as a result. He argued that corruption is not only a government problem; it is common in business too, and fighting it is everyone's responsibility.

For anyone building a career or company, deciding your line in advance makes it easier to hold under pressure. A reputation for integrity takes years to build and can be lost in one deal.
cards.apply_it: Write down one ethical line you won't cross at work, and what you'd say if someone asked you to cross it.

quiz.question: What point did Masiyiwa make about corruption?
options: It also happens in business, and everyone must resist it
quiz.explanation: He said some of the worst corruption he saw was in the private sector and urged personal responsibility.

cards.title: Don't confuse a flashy lifestyle with business success
cards.body:
Masiyiwa has warned young people against measuring success by luxury cars, designer watches and holidays shown online. Display isn't the same as a business that lasts.

He noted that many genuinely wealthy people he met lived simply, with their wealth showing in their investments rather than their clothes. Focusing on building something solid, and meeting responsibilities like children's education first, matters more than looking successful.
cards.apply_it: Pick one thing you spend on mainly to look successful, and redirect that money to your business or savings for a month.

quiz.question: According to Masiyiwa, where did the wealth of many rich people he met show up?
quiz.explanation: He observed that real wealth often sits quietly in investments, not in visible luxuries.

cards.title: Keep investing in your own skills
cards.body:
A theme of the lessons Masiyiwa shares from his own career is to set aside time and money to improve yourself, through training, reading and learning new skills, even when you're passed over or nobody is paying for it.

He also encourages young people to value practical, skilled trades and skills-based businesses rather than only buying and reselling goods. Skills are an asset no one can take from you, and they open opportunities that trading alone can't.
cards.apply_it: Budget a small amount of time and money each month for one course, book or skill that would make you more valuable.

quiz.question: What does Masiyiwa advise doing even when you're overlooked for opportunities?
options: Wait for someone to notice you
Keep investing your own time and money in your skills
quiz.explanation: He urges ongoing self-investment, since skills create opportunities regardless of setbacks.
